articles.headline: QB3 Case Keenum, Bears defense shock Eagles in MNF rout
articles.description: Keenum stepped up big in a pressure situation and combined with a defensive gem to lead the Bears past the Eagles.
articles.headlineJa: 第3QBケース・キーナムとベアーズ守備陣、MNFの圧勝でイーグルスを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: プレッシャーがかかる局面でキーナムが見事な活躍を見せ、素晴らしい守備陣の踏ん張りとともにベアーズをイーグルス戦勝利へと導いた。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Before Monday night, 1,009 days had passed since Case Keenum started a regular-season game. But the Chicago Bears' third-string quarterback, who was pressed into action because of injuries to Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent, showed no rust.

The 38-year-old veteran was 24-of-34 for 247 yards and two touchdowns in a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football."

The Bears' defense also played well, holding Philly to 248 total yards and had three takeaways, including picking off two passes from Jalen Hurts.

Chicago Bears (2-1)

What to make of the QB performance: Keenum walked away with a 4-0 record as a starter against Vic Fangio defenses. The passing game looked terrific Monday night as Keenum routinely made big throws to Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland. Keenum finished 11-of-11 with 145 yards and two touchdowns against the blitz, tied for the fourth-most completions without an incompletion in the 20 years ESPN has been tracking blitzes. He also ran in a 1-yard touchdown, his first since the 2019 season (which was four teams ago). The offense didn't just stay afloat in Williams' absence; it thrived with Keenum taking the reins.

Bears receiver Kalif Raymond, who had six receptions for 90 yards and a TD, said Keenum's pregame message instilled confidence in his teammates.

"He was like, 'I may not be a cowboy, but this is definitely not my first rodeo.' A lot of confidence in him, a lot of confidence in himself," Raymond said. "And to be honest, he practices, preps every week, but particularly this week, we didn't expect anything different from him." 

Stat to know: Dillon Thieneman and T.J. Edwards each intercepted a Jalen Hurts pass, and Austin Booker forced a fumble in the red zone, bringing Chicago's takeaway total to 39 since the start of last season (most in the NFL). This is the Bears' eighth game with at least three takeaways since hiring defensive coordinator Dennis Allen in 2025 (most in the NFL in that span). The Bears are 8-0 in those games.

Trend to watch: The Bears' run game hasn't looked the same since facing the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, when Chicago totaled 291 rushing yards (7.5 yards per attempt) en route to 59 points. Since then, the efficiency has declined with 4.3 yards per rush against Minnesota and 3.7 against the Eagles. Last November behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, the Bears' ground game powered a win over the Eagles with 281 rushing yards. Chicago didn't get the help from its run game in Week 3 and still pulled off an impressive win. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: Sunday vs. New York Jets (1 p.m. ET, Fox)

Philadelphia Eagles (2-1)

The assignment was supposed to be easier, facing a third-string quarterback. Instead, the defense got handled in a troubling Eagles performance on both sides of the ball.

articles.headline: Case Keenum drives Chicago to 3 touchdowns as the Bears beat the Eagles 27-7
articles.description: — Case Keenum was on target and on time all night long.
articles.headlineJa: ケース・キーナムが3TDを演出し、ベアーズが27-7でイーグルスを下す
articles.descriptionJa: 約3年ぶりの先発となったケース・キーナムが2つのタッチダウンパスを決め、シカゴ・ベアーズがジェイレン・ハーツ率いるフィラデルフィア・イーグルスを抑え込んでマンデーナイトで27-7の勝利を収めた。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Case Keenum was on target and on time all night long.


              It turns out the third-string quarterback for the Chicago Bears is pretty good, too.


              Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first start in almost three years, and the Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.


              Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum was 24 for 34 for 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a 1-yard plunge with 7:19 left, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.


              “He knows where everyone is supposed to be on every single play and so he is really quick to recognize coverage,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “He knows why we’re calling the play and what we’re looking for and if we’re not getting that he’s accelerating through it really quickly. That’s what you get when you’re 15-plus years playing that position in this league.”


              It was Keenum’s first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland on Dec. 24, 2023. Williams was sidelined by a right hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent backed up Keenum after he cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


              “To get a shot again like this? Yeah, you dream of it,” Keenum said. “That’s why I'm still here doing this when I get knocked down. I got knocked down my whole career. I just keep getting up, coming to work, just keep bouncing back.”


              Kalif Raymond had six receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown as Chicago (2-1) rebounded from an ugly 9-3 loss to Minnesota.


              Philadelphia (2-1) turned the ball over three times and failed to record a takeaway for the third consecutive game to begin the season. Hurts was 16 for 25 for 153 yards, and Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards on 15 carries.


              “I think we all have to own that loss right there,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. “I don’t think anybody coached well. I don’t think anyone played well. It was a true team loss. And when it’s a true team loss, you know I have to look at myself first.”


              Down 20-7, the Eagles lined up to go for it on fourth-and-1 at their own 49 with about four minutes left in the third quarter. But Hurts was unable to draw a flag for offside, and the Eagles took a delay-of-game penalty before punting it away.


              Hurts was picked off by T.J. Edwards on a fourth-and-5 play from the Chicago 46 in the final minute of the third. Edwards dropped a potential interception on third down on Philadelphia’s first drive of the second half.


              “I liked the decision to go for it on fourth-and-5,” Sirianni said. “Hindsight, I feel like I should have went for it on that fourth-and-1 1/2.”

articles.headline: 'I love this game': Ben Simmons rejects NBA criticism
articles.description: A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.
articles.body:
A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.

The Australian guard is back in the big league this year, having signed a $US3.5 million ($A4.9 million) deal with the Sacramento Kings.

Simmons purchased a controlling stake in a professional sport fishing team and didn't touch a basketball during his year off, in moves that drew plenty of criticism.

But the 30-year-old, who has been ravaged by injuries during his decade-long career, insists the break was purely about rebuilding his physical and mental health.

"It wasn't about if I wanted to play," Simmons told reporters at the Kings' preseason media session on Tuesday (AEST).

"All these people talk about how I don't love the game - that's bull----.

"I love this game. If I didn't, I wouldn't have taken that year to focus on myself and get back to where I'm at."

Simmons added he's not worried by critics chasing clicks from his name, declaring he's ready to prove to the world how much he missed basketball.

"I get to come out here and be creative and play hard and compete against a numerous amount of talented guys, so for me it's just in my blood and I've been doing it since I was a baby."

Simmons - a former No.1 overall draft pick, rookie of the year and three-time All-Star - believes the player he was at his peak "woke up" while he was out of the game.

And he's not short on confidence, bluntly outlining his personal goal this season.

"To dominate. Every time I step on the floor - to dominate," he said.

Simmons last played with the Los Angeles Clippers in April 2025 and took his year off as a result of persistent back and leg injuries, which took a significant toll on his body and mind.

The Melbourne-born star got serious in his comeback bid in August when he flew himself to a player-driven Boomers camp in his home town, where he impressed NBA scouts.

Sacramento pounced, signing Simmons on a one-season veteran league minimum deal.

"I'm right where I need to be," Simmons said.

"I took a lot of time to focus on my body over the season, and I think it's the best decision I've made for my career.

"I'm looking forward to getting going. I feel great, and I'm ready to go. No limitations."

Simmons expects to benefit from the low expectations on himself and the Kings, who were 22-60 last season and have only reached the playoffs once since 2006.

"It's really positive. There's no pressure," he said.

"They don't expect anything from us, so I think for us to go out there and show that we're capable of winning games and having a good team - that's doable.

"Based on this roster, I think we can do that."

Sacramento open the NBA preseason at home against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 5, and visit the Clippers for their regular-season opener on October 21.

articles.headline: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald says team still believes in RB Jadarian Price
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのマイク・マクドナルド監督、チームは今もRBジャダリアン・プライスを信頼していると語る
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのマイク・マクドナルド監督は、ドラフト1巡目指名のルーキーである先発ランニングバックのジャダリアン・プライスが日曜日に2週連続でファンブルロストを喫したものの、チームが彼への信頼を失っていないと述べた。
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row Sunday.

"With JD, he understands what's going on," Macdonald said Monday. "He needs to take care of the ball. I think there's some things fundamentally where we can focus on. We're going to continue to give him the ball. We trust him, and we know he's going to work really hard to do his part as well."

Price's lost fumble in the first quarter Sunday gave the Washington Commanders a short field, setting up their first touchdown. It was one of three turnovers the Seahawks committed in a 33-31 loss that snapped their franchise-record 12-game winning streak.

When Price lost a fumble a week earlier in a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Seahawks went right back to him on the first play of their next drive. But they didn't show the same patience Sunday. After Price's fumble at the 11:06 mark of the first quarter, his next carry wasn't until the 12:49 mark of the third quarter, though he was targeted twice in that span.

Price finished with five carries for 15 yards, plus one catch for 7 yards. Despite making his third straight start, he played 19 of Seattle's 67 offensive snaps, while Emanuel Wilson (nine carries for 14 yards) and George Holani (eight touches for 58 yards) each played 24 snaps.

"I think just, as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Macdonald said postgame. "I know he didn't come back after the initial fumble. We decided to calm it down and bring him back after the half, but he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out. He'll be fine."

Price fumbled five times over three seasons as a backup at Notre Dame.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, have not dealt with this problem in recent years. Kenneth Walker III, whom Price was drafted to replace, fumbled only three times over four seasons with Seattle but did not lose any of them. Zach Charbonnet, who co-started in 2025 alongside Walker, did not fumble over his first three seasons.

Price, who was selected with the 32nd pick, has 119 yards on 28 attempts (4.3 average) over three games, plus four catches for 21 yards. He has yet to score an NFL touchdown.

"JD is such a great, great dude," quarterback Sam Darnold said postgame. "And he knows his responsibility. He knows not to turn the ball over, so there's not much you say to him. You just tell him, 'Keep going, and we've got your back.'"

Macdonald said the Seahawks will decide by Tuesday whether to open Charbonnet's 21-day practice window this week. Charbonnet is on the physically unable to perform list after having ACL surgery in February. He has to spend at least one more game on the PUP list, but he has been eligible to begin practicing as of last week.

articles.headline: Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'
articles.description: Bronny James said he hasn't spoken much to his father, LeBron, about the decision to leave the Lakers this summer, but said he's excited to face him on Christmas.
articles.headlineJa: ブロニー、レブロン・ジェームズのレイカーズ退団に「父には父の道がある」
articles.descriptionJa: ブロニー・ジェームズは、この夏にレイカーズを離れるという父レブロンの決断について本人とあまり話していないとしつつも、クリスマスに対戦するのが楽しみだと語った。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- When LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son and teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So, it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path, and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself, and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So, he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history. Whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father-and-son duo entered the game together or last season in the playoffs, when they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency where the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Bronny James, whose $2.3 million contract for this season is guaranteed, said that he has spent the summer focusing on his role backing up Lakers guards Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Bronny played in 42 games last season and eight playoff games.

"You guys know me as Bronny. My real name is LeBron. I've been doing this for however long," Bronny James said. "It's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron."

Though LeBron and Bronny might not have spoken about the move much, Bronny wishes his father well and is looking forward to the first time the Lakers face the 76ers this season, on Christmas in L.A.

"I'm happy for him and excited to see where their season goes," Bronny James said. "I'm excited to see him on Christmas. I'm excited to play against him on Christmas, so that's going to be good."

Not having LeBron is a significant adjustment for the Lakers and his son. L.A. has nine new players and is trying to focus on this season and not on the past. It is the start of the first season without LeBron since 2017-18.

"It was kind of sad [that he left]; playing with LeBron was amazing," Doncic said about James' departure. "There's a lot of things I learned from him, and we all know who LeBron James is. We spent time together, and it was amazing."
